items.title: Al Grey interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: And it became an Emmy for Fred Astaire and Barrie Chase. And we went out to the studio to do this, in Hollywood

ctx.x: Now in this court, I was the new boy and I’ve just joined the band. So this day that they had Joe Williams on the carpet, I talked to Joe Williams the other day by the way for a half hour, he’s well and everything, and we had some fun talking about many years ago. And why, because Joe Williams, I used to play all the fills for Joe Williams, when Joe would sing. And when I first started doing it I used to have problems doing it. Many years ago when I was with Lionel Hampton they had a blues singer, Sonny Parker,…

if you covered the lyrics, which I really did find out it was very bad. And so that was one of my first lessons. But this now I’m with the band about six days, now they have Joe Williams on the carpet for something that came up. Now they didn’t let me into this meeting, because like I was too new. And I wondered and wondered and wondered, what was going on in this meeting that day. And then finally the case was pretty bad, and Joe Williams lost that case, and the punishment was that he had a very long thing of…
They couldn’t notate the use of the color on the plunger?
